historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly identifies the physical core but treats it as wholly non-runnable and omits the automatable verification path and hardware safety contract.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates manual physical programming from automatable post-boot evidence and uses REQUIRES.
historical_reviews.history: Sequence 538 is the distinct ESC Exit variant.
historical_reviews.v3_1: SF600 may bypass platform protections; a verified read-before-write and chip-level program/verify transcript are mandatory evidence.

original_test_intent: Program the exact board's BIOS flash device with an approved image through an SF600, then prove chip verification, safe restoration, boot recovery and matching BIOS/OS versions.
original_method: A trained operator identifies and isolates the chip, validates adapter/pinout/orientation/voltage and image, reads/preserves the current contents, performs approved erase/program/verify under ESD and power controls, disconnects safely, restores the board, boots and gathers BIOS Setup plus OS/BMC health evidence.
manual_activity: Trained operator performs the physical SF600 hookup, chip read/erase/program/verify, safe disconnect and board restoration; automation can support later version/health evidence. Duplicate ESC is excluded.
required_inputs: SF600 model, software, adapter/clip, pinout, orientation and voltage
safety_requirements: Preserve a verified pre-write chip read
Never connect/disconnect or interrupt in an unsafe state
Stop on contact, identity or verify mismatch
No ESC action, auto-retry or hardware PASS claim
agent_execution_scope: After manual restoration, collect OS/BMC version and health
engineer_actions: Verify BIOS Setup and own final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek correctly refuses ordinary agent hookup but incorrectly imports ESC from duplicate row 361. The readback Script neither drives SF600 nor proves chip verification.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain trained-operator SF600 read/erase/program/verify under the exact vendor hookup and power procedure; automate only artifact checks and post-restoration version/health collection.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SF600 method, reboot, BIOS/OS checks and 30/30-minute timing are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record chip identity, pre-image read hash, exact programmer settings and complete verify transcript, then restore the board before multi-surface boot evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds chip electrical/ESD controls and proof at the programmer layer.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Distinguishes a verified chip write from a later version-only observation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong pinout, voltage, contact or image can damage or brick hardware.

project_override_considerations: Project must approve exact SF600 hardware/software and board-specific hookup; the private version script is post-check only and the duplicate ESC workflow remains separate.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Primary fields consistently request SF600 programming; the readback Script is incomplete rather than contradictory, and duplicate ESC text is isolated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The physical operation is identifiable; the hardware procedure, image, operator, approval and recovery are finite prerequisites. Execution stops rather than guessing any hookup detail.

review_improvement: Defines the chip-level electrical, read-before-write and verify contract while preserving manual physical execution and automatable post-checks.
independent_technical_reasoning: Physical hookup prevents full automation, but it does not make the review permanently blocked: a trained operator can execute the approved SF600 procedure while the agent verifies artifacts and post-boot evidence. That hybrid makes REQUIRES correct instead of DeepSeek NO.
